l4_steps.name: Ingest flight plan, route & forecast winds
l4_steps.input: Active OFP, SIGMET/AIRMET, upper-wind forecast (NWP model)
l4_steps.output: Route profile with fuel-burn model loaded; wind data timestamp recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Wind data currency ≤ 6 hours before STD; 100% OFP retrieval success rate
l4_steps.pain_point: NWP upper-wind refresh is 6-hourly; stale data can inflate or underestimate trip fuel by 2–4%, with no automatic dispatcher alert when forecast age exceeds threshold

l4_steps.name: Calculate trip fuel, alternate & final reserve
l4_steps.input: Route profile, aircraft type/registration, payload estimate, alternate airport selection
l4_steps.output: Trip fuel, alternate fuel, and final reserve fuel (FRF) values in USG/kg
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel calculation accuracy ±1% vs. actual block burn; alternate fuel covers closest suitable alternate per ops spec
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft performance deck must be updated after each engine shop visit or EFW change; stale performance model causes systematic over/under-fuelling accumulating to 0.5–1% fuel cost variance fleet-wide

l4_steps.name: Apply regulatory minimum fuel policy
l4_steps.input: Trip fuel, alternate fuel, FRF; ETOPS/EDTO authorisation if applicable; company fuel policy
l4_steps.output: Regulatory minimum block fuel (FAR 121.639 / ICAO Annex 6 compliant); ETOPS ERA fuel added where required
l4_steps.kpi: 100% regulatory compliance; zero dispatches with sub-minimum fuel on record
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS 180-min routes require En-Route Alternate (ERA) fuel that must be recalculated if the ERA changes post-OFP publication due to NOTAM or weather; no automated re-trigger in Lido when ERA status changes after release

l4_steps.name: Validate fuel load against MTOW & payload limits
l4_steps.system: Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems + Weight & Balance System
l4_steps.input: Planned fuel load, estimated payload (pax + cargo + mail), aircraft MTOW/MLW/MZFW limits
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel quantum; or payload-fuel trade decision with affected bookings flagged
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue payload protection ≥ 95% of booked payload on MTOW-limited sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: MTOW-limited flights at hot/high airports (e.g. LAS in summer, BOG year-round) force late payload offload; no automated interface between Lido and PSS to surface the constraint earlier in the booking cycle

l4_steps.name: Query into-plane fuel prices at origin & destination
l4_steps.system: Aviator Fuel Intelligence (AvFuel) / SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: Flight date, origin/destination ICAO codes, fuel supplier contract references
l4_steps.output: Into-plane fuel price per USG/kg at origin and destination; contract vs. spot price flagged
l4_steps.kpi: Price data latency ≤ 24 hours; contract uplift preference achieved ≥ 95% of uplifts
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel price APIs from major suppliers (BP, Shell, World Fuel Services) vary in latency and data format; feed outages require manual extraction from supplier portals, creating price data gaps that default the model to stale contract rates

l4_steps.name: Model tankering NPV versus weight penalty cost
l4_steps.system: Aviator Fuel Intelligence (AvFuel) / Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems
l4_steps.input: Price differential (origin vs. destination), extra fuel weight, aircraft fuel-burn profile at gross weight
l4_steps.output: Net tankering value in USD per flight; break-even uplift quantity identified
l4_steps.kpi: Tankering model accuracy: positive NPV realised ≥ 90% of cases where model predicted benefit > $150
l4_steps.pain_point: Weight-penalty calculation in simplified models assumes linear burn increase, but penalty is non-linear at high gross weights; simplified model can overstate tankering benefit by 5–10% on heavy flights, leading to sub-optimal decisions

l4_steps.name: Approve or reject tankering uplift quantity
l4_steps.input: Tankering NPV, aircraft structural maximum fuel load, available turnaround time, payload outlook
l4_steps.output: Approved tankering quantity (USG) or 'No tankering' decision recorded with rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Tankering uplift decision issued ≥ 90 minutes before STD; decisions documented 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late payload additions (ULD cargo, late-checked bags) post-tankering approval can invalidate the approved quantity; no automated re-trigger of the tankering model when payload changes after OFP release, requiring manual analyst intervention

l4_steps.name: Finalise planned uplift quantity on OFP
l4_steps.input: Regulatory minimum fuel, tankering decision, captain's discretionary fuel allowance (if pre-authorised)
l4_steps.output: Final planned uplift quantity on signed OFP; fuel release document generated
l4_steps.kpi: Planned vs. actual uplift variance ≤ 2%; OFP fuel release issued ≥ 60 minutes before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher discretionary fuel additions above plan are not consistently documented with a rationale code; absence of structured data makes post-flight fuel efficiency analysis unreliable and prevents feedback into planning model to reduce systematic under-planning

l4_steps.name: Transmit fuel release order to into-plane supplier
l4_steps.input: Fuel release document: planned uplift quantity, aircraft registration, parking stand, STD
l4_steps.output: Fuel order transmitted; supplier acknowledgement received with ETA
l4_steps.kpi: Order transmitted ≥ 60 minutes before fuelling start; supplier ACK received ≤ 15 minutes of transmission
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA FuelsManager integration is absent at smaller outstations, requiring manual phone or fax orders; gaps in electronic audit trail complicate post-flight fuel reconciliation and contract compliance reporting

l4_steps.name: Confirm truck dispatch and stand assignment
l4_steps.input: Fuel order, aircraft stand/gate assignment, turnaround schedule
l4_steps.output: Fuel truck dispatched; confirmed ETA to aircraft stand
l4_steps.kpi: Truck on-stand ≤ 20 minutes before scheduled fuelling start; zero missed fuelling windows due to late truck
l4_steps.pain_point: Late stand changes communicated via AMS cause fuel truck repositioning delays, particularly at congested hub airports; AMS–fuel truck coordination relies on VHF radio and phone at many stations rather than automated system-to-system dispatch

l4_steps.name: Validate fuelling window against turnaround schedule
l4_steps.input: Truck ETA, aircraft block-in time, turnaround milestones, STD
l4_steps.output: Fuelling window confirmed; or expedite request issued to handler with revised fuelling start
l4_steps.kpi: Fuelling completed ≥ 20 minutes before STD; fuelling-related departure delays < 0.5% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-haul turn times (45–60 min) leave minimal buffer; a single fuelling delay cascades directly into a departure delay when there is no concurrent-task optimisation — fuelling, catering, and cleaning compete for the same ramp corridor

l4_steps.name: Perform pre-fuelling fuel quality sample check
l4_steps.system: Fuel Quality Management log (AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware at MRO bases; paper logbook at outstations)
l4_steps.input: Fuel sample drawn from tanker drain or hydrant pit; density meter; water-detection paste
l4_steps.output: Pass/fail quality certificate; density (kg/L) and temperature recorded; release-to-aircraft signed
l4_steps.kpi: 100% pre-fuelling sample compliance; zero aircraft fuelled without a logged pass certificate
l4_steps.pain_point: At outstations with hydrant systems, sample accountability is paper-based and not linked to AMOS; contamination events (water ingress, incorrect fuel grade) have historically been missed — Avianca 052 (1990, fuel exhaustion) and multiple near-misses underscore the cost of manual-only controls at remote stations

l4_steps.name: Execute fuel uplift to planned quantity
l4_steps.system: Fuel truck flow meter / Aircraft fuel gauging system (ACARS uplink)
l4_steps.input: Approved uplift quantity, current fuel-on-board from aircraft gauges, truck flow meter
l4_steps.output: Actual uplift quantity delivered; aircraft fuel gauges confirmed at target level
l4_steps.kpi: Uplift accuracy ±1% of planned quantity; zero over/under-fuelling events per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft fuel gauge tolerance is ±2% on narrow-body types (737/A320); systematic gauge bias, if uncorrected in planning assumptions, causes repeated uplift variance; most fuel planning systems do not ingest gauge correction factors from avionics maintenance records

l4_steps.name: Record actual uplift in tech log and transmit via ACARS
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Telex / SITA ACARS
l4_steps.input: Flow meter final reading, aircraft gauge reading, fueller's delivery receipt
l4_steps.output: Actual uplift entered in aircraft tech log; ACARS fuel completion message sent to OCC and dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS fuel message transmitted ≤ 5 minutes after fuelling complete; tech log discrepancy rate < 1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancy between flow meter and aircraft gauge requires licensed engineer sign-off, adding 5–10 minutes at outstations with limited engineering cover; paper tech logs at regional stations delay OCC visibility into actual fuel state until ACARS message is manually triggered

l4_steps.name: Dispatcher briefs captain on OFP fuel plan & alternates
l4_steps.system: Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems (OFP) + SITA ACARS Datalink
l4_steps.input: Finalised OFP, actual fuel onboard, latest weather update, active NOTAMs, alternate aerodrome status
l4_steps.output: Captain briefed; OFP reviewed and queried or ready for signature
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatcher briefing completed ≥ 30 minutes before STD; zero departures without dispatcher-signed OFP
l4_steps.pain_point: Late weather or NOTAM changes after OFP release require a re-issue; re-issue process in Lido is manual and time-consuming under short turns, creating pressure on dispatchers to release without capturing the latest data

l4_steps.name: Captain accepts or requests additional discretionary fuel
l4_steps.system: Aircraft fuel management panel / Jeppesen FliteDeck Pro (EFB)
l4_steps.input: OFP fuel plan, personal weather/routing assessment, alternate viability, ATC restriction outlook
l4_steps.output: Captain's fuel decision; discretionary addition quantity and rationale (if fuel added)
l4_steps.kpi: Average captain discretionary addition ≤ 5% of trip fuel; additions above 10% flagged for safety review
l4_steps.pain_point: Captain discretionary fuel additions are unstructured — no system captures the stated rationale; without structured data, flight ops cannot distinguish legitimate tactical additions from systematic under-planning, preventing feedback loop improvement in Lido fuel models

l4_steps.name: Finalise load sheet with captain-approved fuel figures
l4_steps.system: Lido/Flight by Lufthansa Systems + Amadeus Altéa PSS (load control module)
l4_steps.input: Captain-approved fuel quantity, actual payload (pax + baggage + cargo), aircraft zero-fuel weight
l4_steps.output: Finalised load sheet signed; OFP fuel figures locked; departure clearance issued to captain
l4_steps.kpi: Load sheet issued ≤ 15 minutes before STD; 100% OFP/load-sheet fuel figure consistency
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual reconciliation between Lido fuel figures and Altéa load control introduces transcription error risk; most carriers lack a direct system interface between flight planning and PSS load control, requiring copy-paste of fuel figures and creating an auditable gap in the data chain

l4_steps.name: Transmit departure fuel state to Operations Control Centre
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS Datalink + OCC Operations Dashboard (AWS-hosted)
l4_steps.input: Final block fuel figures, actual departure time, gate/stand number
l4_steps.output: OCC fuel state record updated; block-off fuel confirmed and archived for post-flight analysis
l4_steps.kpi: OCC fuel state updated ≤ 5 minutes of block-off; 100% ACARS message delivery rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS VHF channel congestion at major hubs (LHR, JFK, LAX) causes message delivery failures during peak pushback windows; manual phone fallback to OCC creates audit gaps in the fuel tracking data stream used for end-of-day fuel efficiency reporting
